name: Guan Muxi
current_role: Listed as linked to Yahgee Modular House (Shenzhen); current role not confirmed
profile: Listed as having made his fortune from Yahgee Modular House, a Shenzhen prefab and modular-building maker. Yahgee went public in Shenzhen in 2009 (002314). A third-party brand listing says Shenzhen Yahgee is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Shenzhen Xinnanshan Holding, the renamed 002314. No source found for his current role.
interesting_fact: Yahgee Modular House raised money by issuing 73.64 million A-shares in a 2009 public offering on the Shenzhen exchange, according to its 2014 fundraising disclosure.

name: Nemish S Shah
current_role: Co-founder, ENAM Holdings (manages treasury and proprietary capital); Governing Body member, FLAME University
profile: Mumbai investor who co-founded ENAM with Vallabh Bhanshali in 1984. ENAM began as a broking firm, then grew into a leading IPO investment bank. ENAM's banking and broking businesses were merged into Axis Bank. Shah now runs ENAM Holdings' treasury and long-term proprietary investing in Indian equities, using bottom-up fundamental research.
interesting_fact: He is widely credited with pioneering equity investment research in India. ENAM's investment banking arm went on to top India's IPO league tables.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a B.Com from Lala Lajpat Rai College (Mumbai University) in 1977. He reads Jain scriptures, follows cricket and loves music, and peers say his spirituality balances his investing.
notes: Very low public profile and no personal social media found. ENAM founders also set up FLAME University in Pune, which may be a warmer route in. No published office email found.

name: Arvind Domadia
current_role: Managing Director, Kunal Structure (India) Pvt Ltd, Ahmedabad (per company registry aggregators)
profile: Gujarat infrastructure contractor. Kunal Structure (India) Pvt Ltd was incorporated in 2006 and builds roads, canals and buildings. A registry aggregator reported operating revenue above INR 500 crore for FY2021. Registry listings name Arvindbhai Amrutlal Domadia as managing director, with his son Kunal A. Domadia as co-director.
interesting_fact: The company carries his son's name, Kunal, who sits on the board with him. Kunal Structure is privately held and was incorporated in April 2006 with registered offices in Bodakdev, Ahmedabad.
notes: Identity based on registry listings only (Arvindbhai Amrutlal Domadia, DIN 01608844). No press coverage, official website or published contacts found. Very private. Kunal Structure also appears in Gujarat tender records.

name: Zheng Dingping
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangdong Great Impression (Dayinxiang) Group, Shantou
profile: Shantou entrepreneur, born 1955 in Chaoyang, who founded Great Impression (大印象) in 1988 and has chaired the group since 1996. The company is best known for health and slimming teas and also makes health products, wine and medicine. It took over Shantou Brewery in 2003 to move into brewing.
interesting_fact: Great Impression expanded beyond health teas by merging with Shantou Brewery in 2003, entering beer brewing. Its range now runs to more than 100 product series.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics by correspondence at Jinan University (1976–77), and in 1994 the Ministry of Agriculture gave him a personal award for scientific and technological progress. He was named a Guangdong Model Worker in 2003.
notes: Bio details come from a user-submitted Chinese directory (maigoo), so verify before use. No official website or published contacts found. Probably best reached through the company in Shantou.

name: Emil D Kakkis
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical (NASDAQ: RARE); founder of the EveryLife Foundation for Rare Diseases
profile: Physician-scientist (MD/PhD, UCLA) who developed Aldurazyme, an enzyme replacement therapy for MPS I, at Harbor-UCLA. As BioMarin's CMO he steered further rare-disease drugs to approval. He founded the EveryLife Foundation in 2009 and Ultragenyx in 2010, and Ultragenyx has built a portfolio of rare and ultra-rare disease therapies.
interesting_fact: Drug companies turned down his MPS I therapy as too complex and too costly for so few patients. The family of a young patient, Ryan Dant, set up the Ryan Foundation and raised the money for the trial, and the drug went on to win FDA approval in 2003.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Montebello and Long Beach, graduated from Pomona College, and did his early MPS enzyme work with Dr. Elizabeth Neufeld. In 2019 he won BIO's Henri A. Termeer Biotechnology Visionary Award.
notes: A frequent public speaker on rare-disease policy, so the EveryLife Foundation is another route. Ultragenyx had an FDA complete response letter for UX111, so check recent company news before outreach. The latest release found (Sept 2025) still listed him as CEO.

name: Madhu N Jain
current_role: Director, IIFL Foundation (CSR arm of IIFL Group); promoter shareholder in IIFL with husband Nirmal Jain
profile: Wife of IIFL founder Nirmal Jain. Together they are promoters of the IIFL financial-services group (IIFL Finance, IIFL Capital, 360 ONE), which Bloomberg has valued their stake in at over $1B. She leads IIFL Foundation, whose flagship Sakhiyon Ki Baadi programme teaches out-of-school girls in rural Rajasthan.
interesting_fact: IIFL Foundation's Sakhiyon Ki Baadi programme has brought about 36,000 out-of-school girls in rural Rajasthan into education, making it one of India's largest girl-literacy efforts. In December 2024 the Foundation adopted 102 government girls' high schools in the state.
deep_cut_fact: She personally received a 'CSR Leadership Award', and the Foundation's work has been recognised by the United Nations. In April 2026 the Foundation opened revitalised government schools in Rajasthan, inaugurated on Mahavir Jayanti.
notes: Her public profile is almost entirely philanthropic (girls' education in Rajasthan). The IIFL Foundation email is the most natural route. Not an operating business executive.

Several Indian company directors share this name, including one at food firms Rich Nutri Foods and Sri Gajpati Foods. I could not tell which, if any, is this person.

name: Thomas S Bremner
current_role: Partner, Venture Growth, Adams Street Partners (Chicago); independent director, BillionToOne (NASDAQ: BLLN)
profile: Chicago growth-equity investor focused on healthcare technology. He joined Adams Street Partners in 2013 after roles at Summit Partners, The Edgewater Funds and JPMorgan Chase. He has served on the board of prenatal and cancer-diagnostics company BillionToOne since 2022, and his reported health-tech investments include DispatchHealth, Lyra Health and VillageMD.
interesting_fact: He has sat on BillionToOne's board since early 2022, before its 2025 Nasdaq IPO. BillionToOne makes molecular diagnostics such as single-molecule prenatal and oncology tests.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at the University of Dayton (BS) before earning an MBA with high honors from Chicago Booth. He is a CFA charterholder and sits on Adams Street's Impact Investment Committee.
notes: Probably on Forbes/SEC lists through Adams Street's BillionToOne stake rather than personal founder wealth. The best route is Adams Street's contact page.

name: Anastasios Arima
current_role: Founder, Managing Director & CEO, IperionX (ASX: IPX / NASDAQ: IPX)
profile: Engineer and entrepreneur known as Taso. He founded Piedmont Lithium (NASDAQ: PLL), now merged into Elevra Lithium, and helped finance and list it on NASDAQ. He now runs IperionX, which makes low-carbon titanium metal from scrap using patented technologies at its Virginia plant and owns the Titan critical-minerals project in Tennessee. IperionX has U.S. Army and defense supply contracts.
interesting_fact: IperionX won its first U.S. Army titanium task order, which Arima called 'a decisive step toward reshoring the nation's titanium supply chain'. Its Virginia facility recycles titanium scrap into 100%-recyclable metal products.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Greece and emigrated to Perth, and holds both a Bachelor of Commerce and a Bachelor of Engineering from the University of Western Australia.
notes: Very relevant to an energy and critical-minerals podcast. He books podcast guest spots through Fame (fame.so speaker page), so he is clearly open to podcast appearances.

name: J. Richard Cashio
current_role: Independent director, ServisFirst Bancshares (chair of Corporate Governance & Nominations Committee); private investor
profile: Birmingham, Alabama industrialist turned private investor, aged 68. He was CEO of Tricon Metals & Services from 2000 until its sale in October 2008, then CEO of TASSCO, LLC until retiring in January 2014. He has been on the ServisFirst Bank board since the bank opened in 2005 and holds about 1% of the bank holding company.
interesting_fact: He is one of ServisFirst's founding directors, on the bank's board since its first day in May 2005. ServisFirst has since grown into a multi-state commercial bank listed on the NYSE.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his bachelor's degree from the University of Alabama in 1979. ServisFirst's proxy says it values him because he brings 'the perspectives of one of our target customer groups' – industrial business owners.
notes: Low public profile, a retired metals-industry CEO. A third-party profile lists him as a director of Children's Harbor (Alabama children's charity). Formal route: the ServisFirst corporate secretary, 2500 Woodcrest Place, Birmingham AL (the director correspondence address in the proxy).
